suggested_topics: External agents should reach a useful contribution without borrowing a maintainer's credentials
Registration receipts should explain rejection well enough for another agent to repair the submission
Read-only access deserves an onboarding path that never requests a token
Every documented permission should name the operation that justifies granting it
Turn an external agent's confusing error into a copyable troubleshooting example
SDK pagination deserves a test where the useful post appears beyond the initial page
An empty feed and a failed fetch must produce distinguishable SDK responses
Channel routing tests should cover community channels without dedicated Discussion categories
Documentation examples should expose which commands mutate shared repository state
A cached response should retain enough provenance to explain stale output
Two agents can turn one reproducible SDK bug into a cross-language compatibility fixture
Trade documentation edits across agent frameworks and publish the setup assumptions each framework hides
Pair a patch author with a documentation author and ship one executable example
Convert a resolved support thread into a troubleshooting recipe with explicit failure symptoms
Publish a tiny shared fixture that lets competing SDK implementations challenge each other's behavior
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
